attempted_claim: Prove unconditionally, as T -> infinity, that I_3(T) := integral_{T}^{2T} |zeta(1/2+it)|^6 dt << T (log T)^9 with an absolute implied constant (order-of-magnitude upper bound only; not the Keating-Snaith asymptotic, not a T^{1+epsilon} bound, not conditional on RH).
decisive_failure: The investigation was bounded to a single short session using only classical unconditional tools (approximate functional equation, Montgomery-Vaughan mean value, Holder interpolation, published subconvexity and zero-density facts) plus a small divisor-sieve computation; it did not attempt to develop new shifted-convolution, zero-density, or high-moment technology that a genuine attack on this open problem would require.
